title: U.S. House · Washington's 1st District
area: Northeastern King County and Snohomish County suburbs, including Redmond, Kirkland, Woodinville, Bothell and Sammamish.

context.text: Suzan DelBene and Mary Silva advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary. DelBene won the primary with 54.5% of the vote to Silva's 27.2%, out of six candidates on the ballot.

candidates.name: Suzan DelBene
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 top-two primary with 54.5% of the vote

summary.text: Suzan DelBene is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 1st District, first elected in 2012. Before Congress she was a technology executive and entrepreneur and then director of the Washington State Department of Revenue. She serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and chaired the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee for the 2024 cycle.

background.text: Born in Selma, Alabama, in 1962. According to her official biography, she spent part of her early childhood in Newport Hills and Mercer Island, Washington, before her family moved around the country in search of work after her father lost his job.
Earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Reed College in 1983 and an MBA from the University of Washington in 1990.

Began her career in immunology research, according to her official biography, before moving into business. She spent 12 years at Microsoft, most recently as corporate vice president of its mobile communications business, and, according to her official biography, helped start drugstore.com.
Served as CEO and president of Nimble Technology, a business software company based on technology developed at the University of Washington. Also worked as a consultant for Global Partnerships.

Served as director of the Washington State Department of Revenue. Her official biography says she proposed reforms to cut red tape for small businesses and enacted a tax amnesty program that generated $345 million.
Ran for Congress in Washington's 8th District in 2010 and lost to incumbent Republican Dave Reichert.

Won a special election in 2012 to fill the remainder of Jay Inslee's term and the regular election for the redrawn 1st District, and was first sworn in to the House in November 2012. Has been re-elected since.

Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and its Tax, Trade, and Oversight subcommittees. Co-chairs the Women's High-Tech Coalition, Kidney Caucus, and MedTech Caucus, and chaired the New Democrat Coalition in the 117th Congress.
Appointed by House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in December 2022 as chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee for the 2024 election cycle.
Her official biography lists among her legislative accomplishments two laws addressing the baby formula shortage and the National Landslide Preparedness Act.

priorities.text: As the former director of the Washington State Department of Revenue, DelBene says she knows firsthand how important it is to have a tax code that is predictable, easy to navigate, and fair for hardworking families and small businesses.
DelBene's housing platform notes that housing prices in King County have increased by more than 200% since 2012, leaving many Washingtonians with limited access to affordable housing.
On reproductive rights, DelBene states: "I firmly believe that women should make their own health care decisions—not politicians."
priorities.quote: I firmly believe that women should make their own health care decisions—not politicians.

positions.summary: Supports legal access to abortion, saying health care decisions should be made by women, not politicians.
positions.quote: I firmly believe that women should make their own health care decisions—not politicians.

positions.summary: Says the nation must build a new economy based on clean and renewable energy while reducing dependence on fossil fuels and foreign oil.
Says she is committed to ensuring all Americans have access to affordable, quality health care and to expanding access for the most vulnerable populations.
Identifies the region's housing-affordability crisis as a priority, citing more than 200% price growth in King County since 2012.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Ways and Means for the 2025-2026 Congress, including its Oversight, Tax, and Trade subcommittees.

candidates.name: Mary Silva
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary with 27.2% of the vote

summary.text: Mary Silva is the Republican candidate for Washington's 1st District and an audiologist who has worked in the field for about two decades. She ran in the 2024 top-two primary for the same seat, finishing fourth with 6.5% of the vote, and advanced to the general election in 2026 with 27.2%. In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she says her campaign focuses on national security and technology supply chains, taxes and housing costs, and government transparency.

background.text: Graduated from Richland High School. Earned a bachelor's degree from Western Washington University in 2003, a graduate degree from Washington State University in 2006, and a Doctor of Audiology from Salus University in 2009.
Has worked as an audiologist; in a 2024 survey response she said she had done so in Washington State for 19 years, and she has been affiliated with the Washington State Academy of Audiology.
Describes herself as a wife, mother, and Christian who volunteers as a board member of her professional state organization and at her child's school (2024 survey response).

Says her path to public service began when she sent research on offshored chip and software manufacturing and foreign espionage risk to her congresswoman and state lawmakers, and did not get meetings with them (2026 survey response).
Ran in the August 6, 2024 top-two primary for Washington's 1st District as a Republican and did not advance, receiving 6.5% of the vote (11,339 votes).
Advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary with 27.2% of the vote, behind incumbent Suzan DelBene.

priorities.text: Silva says Washington's cost of living has risen due to inflation and a housing shortage, and calls for rewarding local governments that streamline permitting and capping investor purchases of single-family homes.
Says she wants to "cut middle-class taxes, deregulate, slash green energy mandates, and expand domestic energy production to lower costs and increase take-home pay."
priorities.quote: cut middle-class taxes, deregulate, slash green energy mandates, and expand domestic energy production to lower costs and increase take-home pay

priorities.text: States her highest priority in the House would be pressing for public hearings into the alleged involvement of Israeli and other foreign intelligence agencies in the September 11, 2001 attacks, and reforming FISA court rules and whistleblower protections.

positions.summary: Says taxing the wealthy "hasn't improved middle-class take-home pay" and calls for cutting middle-class taxes instead.
positions.quote: Taxing the wealthy hasn't improved middle-class take-home pay.

positions.summary: Supports rewarding local governments that streamline permitting to increase housing supply and lower costs.
Calls for slashing "green energy mandates" and expanding domestic (including fossil fuel) energy production.

researchNotes: DelBene's Ballotpedia page had no 2026 campaign-themes text, so her priorities and positions come from her official House issues page, which is not dated to this cycle specifically. Silva's positions are drawn from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, which includes claims about foreign intelligence involvement in 9/11 that are reported here as her stated views, not verified facts. Silva has no official or news biography beyond her Ballotpedia pages, so her biography relies on her own survey responses; no campaign website URL was recorded for her.
